It overlaps with aged ozonated-charcoal water, but the two don't always work equally. Sometimes DMSO calms a trip better, and sometimes the charcoal water does. I don't yet know why. In my experience there is generally no harm in taking both or mixing them. Ozonated-charcoal water has what I consider a perfect safety profile; DMSO is a close second in my experience.

Niacin flush: itchy sunburn-like heat. The flush is normal, although some people find it intolerable and others enjoy it.
Heartburn in sensitive stomachs or after too much at once.
Drowsiness, usually with terrible sleep quality.
Higher or repeated doses can create a real risk of liver damage, especially with liver problems, alcohol, or medications.

Other forms of vitamin B3 seem less reliable than niacin for relaxation. Niacinamide relaxes some people, but it can make others hyperfocused, depending on the state the person is in. Avoid sustained-release niacin and the useless "no-flush" kind (inositol hexanicotinate).

Shadow work to me is neither BDSM nor "feeding your demons." It means bringing loving awareness to the parts of the mind built in fear, pain, humiliation, rejection, and survival. Inner-child reparenting is central to shadow work. Most negative mind-states aren't some error in your philosophy, they're just young parts of you that are still waiting for love and protection and permission, and for the explanation nobody ever gave them.

Relax, unwind, unbind, and unweave the identity illusion, mind, and unified experience. My pamphlet on already-perfect goes further into this.

I am not repeating the simplistic Hermetic claim that opposites are required to understand anything. A hated baby does not feel love, and a loved baby does not feel hate. In the subconscious world of concepts, though, each idea often comes paired with its opposite.
